scope: Pediatric outpatient/home medication regimens after ED/urgent-care evaluation
safety_rules: Select regimen by diagnosis; never copy a dose across indications.
Liquid mL may be generated only from an explicitly verified exact product concentration.
Apply source adult/per-dose and daily caps.
Weight basis is explicit. Do not substitute actual/ideal/adjusted weight silently.
Marked obesity requires drug-specific review when evidence is limited; adult maximums still apply when the source specifies them.
Renal/hepatic impairment, allergy, drug interactions, inability to tolerate oral treatment, red flags and age restrictions may override outpatient treatment.

obesity_policy.rule: For patients <18 years and <40 kg, weight-based dosing is generally used. At >=40 kg, continue weight-based dosing unless it exceeds the recommended adult dose for the indication. Drug-specific PK/weight-scalar evidence supersedes this general rule.
obesity_policy.explicit_exception: RCH oral paracetamol is dosed on ideal body weight.
obesity_policy.note: Do not assign ideal or adjusted body weight to other outpatient drugs without drug-specific evidence.

entries.diagnosis: mild/moderate pain or fever in a child >1 month suitable for home treatment
entries.frequency: every 6 h as needed; minimum interval 4 h
entries.administration: May be taken with or without food. Shake suspension. Avoid all other paracetamol/acetaminophen-containing products.
entries.source: RCH Acute Pain Management 2024; current paracetamol SmPC 120 mg/5 mL

entries.diagnosis: mild/moderate pain or fever when NSAID is appropriate
entries.frequency: every 6-8 h as needed; home schedule capped at 3 doses/day
entries.administration: Give with food; use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration.

excluded_patient_flags.message: avoid ibuprofen in dehydration because of renal risk
avoid/seek specialist dosing advice in significant renal impairment
contraindicated with active/recurrent peptic ulcer or GI bleeding

entries.source: RCH Acute Pain Management 2024; ibuprofen 100 mg/5 mL SmPC

entries.diagnosis: persistent nausea/vomiting with gastroenteritis to support oral rehydration; child >6 months
entries.administration: Adjunct to oral rehydration only. Improvement in vomiting does not exclude serious disease.
cautions: bilious vomiting or surgical red flags

entries.diagnosis: isolated acute urticaria without anaphylaxis, age 6-11 months
entries.administration: Use a non-sedating antihistamine. Avoid NSAIDs as they can worsen urticaria.
cautions: any airway/respiratory/circulatory or significant GI involvement = evaluate for anaphylaxis
entries.source: RCH Urticaria; current cetirizine product concentration

entries.diagnosis: isolated acute urticaria/allergic symptoms, age >=1 year
entries.administration: May be given as oral solution. Avoid NSAIDs in acute urticaria if they worsen symptoms.
cautions: anaphylaxis features require adrenaline pathway, not antihistamine alone

entries.diagnosis: allergic rhinitis or urticaria, age >=2 years
entries.administration: Oral syrup. In severe hepatic impairment use the product-label reduced initial frequency rather than this standard regimen.

entries.diagnosis: allergic rhinitis or urticaria, age >=1 year
seasonal allergic rhinitis when fexofenadine selected
entries.administration: For the 120 mg adolescent tablet regimen, take before a meal. Product/age licensing varies; verify exact product.

entries.diagnosis: moderately severe/severe asthma exacerbation suitable for discharge, age <2 years
entries.administration: Give according to written asthma discharge plan; food may reduce GI upset if product permits.

entries.diagnosis: moderately severe/severe asthma exacerbation suitable for discharge, age 2-5 years
acute asthma exacerbation suitable for discharge, age 6-11 years
acute asthma exacerbation when dexamethasone strategy selected
croup with stridor/risk features suitable for outpatient management after assessment
asthma/wheeze discharge reliever via pMDI + spacer under written asthma action plan
entries.frequency: per written asthma action plan; urgent review if reliever is required again within 4 h after discharge
entries.administration: One puff at a time through spacer with correct technique. Ensure written action plan and controller review.
entries.source: RCH asthma discharge education; GINA 2026 acute asthma

entries.diagnosis: acute otitis media when antibiotic treatment is indicated
entries.administration: May be taken with or without food; follow exact product label. Complete the prescribed course.

entries.diagnosis: mild community-acquired pneumonia treated as outpatient
dental abscess requiring antibiotic plus dental/surgical management
entries.administration: Antibiotic does not replace definitive dental/surgical treatment.

entries.diagnosis: infected/high-risk bite suitable for oral outpatient therapy

verified_concentrations.label: 400/57 mg per 5 mL; amoxicillin component 80 mg/mL

entries.administration: Give at the start of a meal; shake suspension before each dose.
entries.source: RCH antimicrobial bite regimen + co-amoxiclav 400/57 mg/5 mL SmPC

entries.diagnosis: periorbital/orbital cellulitis oral step-down after appropriate initial assessment/treatment
entries.administration: Give at the start of a meal. Not a substitute for orbital-cellulitis imaging/specialist/inpatient pathway when indicated.

entries.diagnosis: mild/moderate cellulitis suitable for oral outpatient therapy
entries.administration: May be given without regard to meals. Reassess if rapidly progressive or systemic illness.
cautions: marked renal impairment requires dose review

entries.diagnosis: mild preseptal cellulitis in a well child
uncomplicated lower UTI/cystitis in a child >3 months who is not systemically unwell
pyelonephritis in selected child <12 months suitable for oral regimen per local pathway
cautions: young infant threshold for admission/IV treatment

entries.diagnosis: pyelonephritis age >=12 months suitable for oral outpatient therapy
cautions: systemic illness may require IV/inpatient care

entries.diagnosis: mild MRSA-suspected/confirmed skin infection when TMP-SMX selected

verified_concentrations.label: 40 mg TMP/200 mg SMX per 5 mL; TMP 8 mg/mL

entries.administration: Dose expressed as trimethoprim component. Taking with food or drink may reduce GI upset.
entries.source: RCH Antimicrobial guidelines; Co-Trimoxazole pediatric suspension SmPC 2026

entries.diagnosis: mild MRSA skin infection when clindamycin selected
entries.administration: Give with a full glass of water when age-appropriate; monitor for antibiotic-associated diarrhea/colitis.

entries.diagnosis: pertussis treatment/prophylaxis regimen in infant <6 months
entries.administration: Once daily, with or without food; immediately before a meal may improve GI tolerability. Shake suspension.
entries.source: RCH Antimicrobial guidelines; azithromycin 200 mg/5 mL SmPC 2026

entries.diagnosis: pertussis treatment/prophylaxis regimen age >=6 months
entries.administration: Once daily, with or without food; immediately before a meal may improve GI tolerability. Shake suspension.
entries.source: RCH Antimicrobial guidelines; azithromycin 200 mg/5 mL SmPC 2026

entries.diagnosis: pertussis when clarithromycin selected, age >=1 month
entries.administration: May be given without regard to meals; food/drink after the suspension can reduce bitter aftertaste.
cautions: renal impairment may require dose reduction
entries.source: RCH antimicrobial pertussis regimen; clarithromycin 125 mg/5 mL SmPC

entries.diagnosis: pertussis when macrolide cannot be used, age >6 weeks

verified_concentrations.label: TMP 8 mg/mL in 40/200 mg per 5 mL suspension

entries.administration: Dose expressed as trimethoprim component. May be preferable with food/drink to reduce GI upset.
entries.source: RCH antimicrobial pertussis regimen; Co-Trimoxazole SmPC

entries.diagnosis: lower UTI/cystitis, NICE short-course variant
entries.administration: Take with food or milk; shake suspension.

minimum_patient_values.message: nitrofurantoin outpatient regimen requires eGFR >=45 mL/min in this module

excluded_patient_flags.message: nitrofurantoin is contraindicated in G6PD deficiency in the cited SmPC
nitrofurantoin is contraindicated in acute porphyria
nitrofurantoin must not be used for pyelonephritis/renal parenchymal infection

entries.source: NICE NG109 short-course lower UTI regimen; nitrofurantoin 25 mg/5 mL SmPC for product/food/contraindications

entries.diagnosis: acute lower UTI using current 25 mg/5 mL SmPC course
entries.administration: Take with food or milk; shake suspension.

minimum_patient_values.message: nitrofurantoin is contraindicated below eGFR 45 mL/min in this SmPC regimen

entries.diagnosis: influenza treatment in infant <1 year when antiviral treatment indicated
influenza treatment age >=1 year when antiviral treatment indicated
anaphylaxis discharge plan when auto-injector is indicated

bands.device: 500 microgram device may be considered in adolescents >12 years where locally available; 300 microgram device remains product/pathway dependent

entries.administration: Provide two devices when indicated, device training, written anaphylaxis action plan and allergy referral. IM adrenaline remains first-line for recurrent anaphylaxis.

entries.diagnosis: localized impetigo suitable for topical therapy
entries.topical_instructions: Apply mupirocin 2% to affected area three times daily for 5 days.

entries.diagnosis: acute otitis media when antibiotic treatment is indicated and penicillin allergy/intolerance requires a macrolide alternative
entries.administration: May be taken with or without food. Verify exact suspension strength; important CYP3A/QT interactions apply.
contraindications: concomitant contraindicated QT/CYP3A interacting medicines per SmPC
entries.source: NICE NG91 acute otitis media, amended 2022; clarithromycin SmPC for product use

entries.diagnosis: acute sinusitis in a child when immediate/back-up antibiotic is indicated and first-choice penicillin is appropriate
entries.administration: Use exact product instructions. Oral penicillin V absorption is reduced by food for many products; follow the exact SmPC and preferably dose away from meals when specified.
cautions: renal impairment may require interval review
severe systemic/orbital/intracranial features require hospital pathway

entries.diagnosis: acute sinusitis requiring antibiotic in child with penicillin allergy/intolerance
entries.administration: May be taken with or without food; verify exact formulation.

entries.diagnosis: community-acquired pneumonia in child when oral macrolide is selected for penicillin allergy/intolerance or atypical pathogen coverage
entries.administration: May be taken with or without food; verify exact product and interaction profile.
entries.source: NICE NG250 pneumonia; RCH CAP allergy pathway

entries.diagnosis: impetigo that is extensive or unsuitable for localized topical therapy
entries.administration: Can be taken without regard to meals; verify exact SmPC.

entries.diagnosis: mild bacterial cervical lymphadenitis suitable for oral outpatient therapy
preschool asthma age 1-5 years requiring first-line preventer treatment
entries.administration: Use pMDI with spacer; facemask until coordinated with mouthpiece. Rinse mouth/brush teeth after ICS where feasible. Review control and technique.
cautions: step down to lowest effective dose

entries.diagnosis: preschool asthma age 1-5 years when LTRA is chosen as alternative/adjunct preventer
entries.administration: Chewable/granule product depends on age and local product. Stop and review if agitation, sleep disturbance, mood or behavioral changes occur.
entries.source: RCH Preschool asthma; INFARMED confirms 4 mg pediatric chewable presentations in Portugal

entries.diagnosis: asthma age 6-11 years, Step 2 low-dose ICS preventer
entries.administration: Use prescribed inhaler correctly; review adherence, technique and control before step-up.
entries.source: RCH asthma in primary school-aged children

entries.diagnosis: asthma age 6-11 years, Step 2 low-dose ICS preventer
entries.administration: Use spacer with pMDI when appropriate; rinse mouth after ICS. Check adherence and technique before step-up.
entries.source: RCH asthma in primary school-aged children

entries.diagnosis: asthma age 6-11 years when montelukast is selected as alternative/adjunct controller
entries.administration: Review for agitation, sleep disturbance or altered mood and stop/reassess if these occur.
entries.source: RCH asthma 6-11 years; INFARMED pediatric 5 mg chewable presentations

entries.diagnosis: asthma age 6-11 years, Step 3 ICS/LABA maintenance option
entries.frequency: twice daily maintenance; reliever strategy must match written plan
entries.administration: Controller regimen only. Confirm whether separate SABA or MART strategy is being used; do not mix plans silently.
entries.source: RCH asthma in primary school-aged children

entries.diagnosis: asthma age 6-11 years using GINA 2026 AIR/MART strategy with the specified low-dose budesonide-formoterol formulation

bands.step3: 1 inhalation once daily plus 1 as needed
bands.step4: 1 inhalation twice daily plus 1 as needed

entries.administration: Use only the specified ICS-formoterol strength/device suitable for AIR/MART. Seek medical care if >8 total inhalations are needed in 24 h.

entries.diagnosis: asthma age 12-17 years using GINA 2026 AIR/MART strategy

bands.step3: 1 inhalation twice (or once) daily plus 1 as needed
bands.step4_5: 2 inhalations twice daily plus 1 as needed

entries.administration: AIR/MART only with an appropriate ICS-formoterol product. Seek medical care if >12 total inhalations are needed in 24 h.

expansion_notes: Block A: diagnosis-specific antibiotic alternatives and asthma controller strategies; GINA 2026/RCH/NICE; Portugal concentrations only where independently verified.
